addressed.problem: `add` accepts an empty `participants` list and stores the expense. `balances()` then calls `split(cents, 0)`, which raises ValueError. One bad add leaves the ledger permanently unable to compute balances, and a later `settle` has nothing to work on. This breaks the rule that a failed add changes nothing and that validation happens before any state change.
addressed.evidence: ledger.py:38-47: `names = [...]` is an empty list, `len(set(names)) == len(names)` holds, and the Expense is appended. `ledger.add('2026-01-05','Ann','10.00',[])` succeeds. After that, `balances()` hits split(1000, 0) in money.py:25 and raises ValueError('parts must be at least 1').
addressed.fix: In `add`, raise ValueError when `names` is empty, before building the Expense and appending it. Add a test for it.
addressed.if_skipped: Any caller that passes an empty participant list corrupts the ledger. Every later `balances()` call fails, including calls with a date range that excludes that expense only if it lies outside the range, so the failure depends on the dates.

plan: Baseline: tests (34) and acceptance (19) all pass.
Contracts/integration: ledger -> balances -> settle zeroes everyone within len-1 transfers; monthly balances via months_between sum to the total (qa/test_qa.py, passing).
Edge/errors: odd amounts and dates (unicode digits, newline, '+1', '1.'), failed add leaves the ledger unchanged, empty participants rejected, split sums, settle does not mutate its input (passing).
Limits: calendar end (D2) and an inverted balances period. D2 tests stay red on purpose (low severity).
Regression, non-functional: discarded, since there was no prior code and the architecture sets no security or performance requirements.

defects.repro: month_end(date(9999,12,10)) and months_between(date(9999,12,1), date(9999,12,1)) raise ValueError('year 10000 is out of range'). The contract says the first returns 9999-12-31 and the second returns one clipped period.
defects.fix: In month_end, compute the last day without building the next month's first day, e.g. calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]. Make months_between stop when first.month==12 and first.year==9999.
defects.if_skipped: Only dates in December 9999 fail, so the practical effect is negligible.
